***

## Goal

Build a tiny Spring Boot app that responds to:

```text
GET http://localhost:8080/hello  →  Hello World
```

You will type every step in your IDE. Pause the video and implement here — that is the point of these notes.

***

## Concepts you need while coding

### Localhost, IP, and port

| Idea | Plain meaning |
|------|----------------|
| **IP address** | Unique address of a machine on a network |
| **localhost / 127.0.0.1** | “This same computer” |
| **Port** | Number that routes traffic to *one* process on that machine (Chrome, Spotify, your app…) |
| **Default Spring Boot port** | `8080` (changeable) |

On the public internet, browsers often hit **443** (HTTPS). A reverse proxy may forward that to your app’s internal port (e.g. 8080). Locally you call the app port directly.

### Spring Initializr

[start.spring.io](https://start.spring.io/) generates a **ready project skeleton**: folders, Java version, Spring Boot version, and `pom.xml` dependencies — so you are not stuck on setup before writing business code.

### Embedded Tomcat

Adding **Spring Web** pulls in an **embedded Apache Tomcat**. When you run the main class, Tomcat listens on a port. You do not install Tomcat separately for this hello-world.

### Annotations you will use (names only — depth later)

| Annotation | Role in this lecture |
|------------|----------------------|
| `@SpringBootApplication` | On the generated main class — Boot entry point |
| `@RestController` | Marks a class as an HTTP API “gateway” |
| `@GetMapping("/hello")` | Maps HTTP GET `/hello` to a method |

***

## Practice — build it step by step

### Step 0 — prerequisites

- JDK installed
- IDE ready
- Video paused after the Initializr section if you prefer typing first

### Step 1 — generate the project

1. Open [https://start.spring.io](https://start.spring.io/)
2. Choose roughly:

| Field | Suggested choice |
|-------|------------------|
| Project | **Maven** |
| Language | **Java** |
| Spring Boot | A **stable** release (avoid `SNAPSHOT` / `RC` while learning) |
| Packaging | **Jar** |
| Java | **21** (or 17+) |
| Dependencies | **Spring Web** |

3. Click **Generate**, unzip the project, open the folder in your IDE.

::: {.callout-note}
Exact Boot version numbers change over time. Prefer the newest **stable** release Initializr offers. Concepts stay the same.
:::

### Step 2 — run the skeleton once

Open the generated `*Application.java` (has `public static void main`).

Optionally add one line inside `main` **before** understanding Boot:

```java
System.out.println("Hello World");
```

Run the main class. In the console logs you should see something like **Tomcat started on port(s): 8080**.

Open a browser:

```text
http://localhost:8080
```

You will likely see a **Whitelabel Error Page** — that is OK. It proves the server is up, but no endpoint is mapped yet.

### Step 3 — create `HelloController`

In the same package as your main application class (e.g. `com.example.demo`), create:

```java
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.GetMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RestController;

@RestController
public class HelloController {

    @GetMapping("/hello")
    public String hello() {
        return "Hello World";
    }
}
```

**What you are doing**

- `@RestController` → “this class exposes HTTP endpoints”
- `@GetMapping("/hello")` → “when someone GETs `/hello`, run this method”
- Returning a `String` → Spring writes that string as the HTTP response body

### Step 4 — verify in the browser

1. Re-run the application (restart so changes load).
2. Visit:

```text
http://localhost:8080/hello
```

Expected: page shows `Hello World`.

### Step 5 — change the port

Open `src/main/resources/application.properties` and add:

```properties
server.port=9090
```

Restart. Tomcat should start on **9090**. Now:

```text
http://localhost:8080/hello   → fails (nothing listening)
http://localhost:9090/hello   → Hello World
```

Set the port back to `8080` (or delete the line) when you are done experimenting.

### Step 6 — second endpoint

Add another method (method name does **not** have to match the path):

```java
@GetMapping("/bye")
public String greetBye() {
    return "Bye";
}
```

Restart and test both `/hello` and `/bye`.

### Step 7 — optional HTML in the response

```java
@GetMapping("/hello")
public String hello() {
    return "<h1>Hello World</h1>";
}
```

The browser will render the heading. (Real apps usually return JSON and let a frontend render HTML — that comes later.)

***

## Mental model after this lecture

```text
Browser  --GET /hello-->  Embedded Tomcat (port 8080)
                              |
                              v
                         Spring MVC mapping
                              |
                              v
                         HelloController.hello()
                              |
                              v
                         "Hello World" response body
```

You have **not** yet learned *how* mapping works internally. That is intentional. Lecture 1–2 show the destination; later lectures open the engine.

## Exercises

1. Add `GET /ping` that returns `pong`.
2. Change `server.port` to `7070` and update your browser URL.
3. Temporarily remove `@RestController`, restart, hit `/hello` — what happens? Put it back.
4. Write three bullet points: What did Initializr save you from doing by hand?
